subject: EdgeRep pilot — burst SLA exemption & capacity sidecar questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & sidecar capacity ask

Team — quick context: EdgeRep (fast-growing edge caching vendor) is ready to start a 6-week pilot next month. They want sub-50ms tail latency for inference at specific metropolitan PoPs; their traffic will spike unpredictably during live demos and launches. They asked whether we can guarantee a short-term burst SLA (guaranteed GPU slice availability for demo windows) and a capacity sidecar to isolate their pilot from noisy neighbors.

Key asks from Sales/Customer:
- Temporary dedicated slice + burst lane for peak demos (2–4 hours several times per week)
- Autoscale policy that allows aggressive burst beyond standard quota for 1–2 weeks during launch
- Quick confirmation that KV-cache warming and prefix caching can be pre-seeded to avoid cold starts

I'm copying product, infra, and procurement for feasibility and ops/runbook requirements. Attaching the draft SLA they sent and our preliminary capacity workbook.

Next steps I'd like: short feasibility note from infra (what we can support), product impact assessment (any model/feature gating), and procurement guidance on contract language for an exception.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: edgerep-sla-draft.pdf, edgepilot-capacity-plan.xlsx
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & sidecar capacity ask

Thanks Marissa — quick follow-ups from product side so we scope correctly:

1) Workload profile: do we have expected qps/peak tokens per second per PoP? The workbook lists regional RPS but not peak token-latency pairings. For tight tail latency we need sequence-length distribution and percentiles.

2) Model variants: is EdgeRep asking to pin a specific model (and quantization level) or will they accept a lower-precision variant during bursts? If we can swap to an aggressively quantized variant as fallback we can reduce resource needs.

3) Cache seeding: we can pre-seed KV-cache for warm prefixes, but doing so across multiple PoPs requires orchestration and a pre-warm window. How many unique prefixes per demo?

Jonas — can you outline constraints (slice size, pre-warm window, expected pre-seed bandwidth) and any manual ops we need to coordinate?

Soojing/Kim — procurement/product: any constraints on making an SLA exception for a pilot? If we allow burst lanes, do we want explicit penalty-free opt-out clauses after the pilot?

I'll consolidate answers and propose a minimal runbook for demos.

— Priyom
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & sidecar capacity ask

Priyom / team — technical feasibility notes below. TL;DR: achievable with caveats and a short ops window.

Constraints and proposed approach:
- Dedicated slice sizing: for sub-50ms tail we need a minimum N=4 A100-equivalent concurrent slots per PoP for the model they're targeting (assuming 512 token sequences). If we can accept a heavily quantized 4-bit variant for demos, that reduces to N=2.

- Burst lane behavior: we can carve a burst pool (hot spare slices) that can be attached to the tenant for scheduled windows. That pool should be reserved at least 4 hours before the demo for KV-cache pre-warm. On-demand immediate spikes without warm time will show higher cold-start latencies.

- Autoscale policy exception: we can add an override that temporarily raises the per-tenant ceiling and reduces cooldown windows, but this bypasses global smoothing heuristics. That increases risk of noisy neighbor impact and transient higher infra spend. We can mitigate by limiting burst windows to predefined calendar blocks and a maximum aggregate token cap.

- Pre-seed bandwidth: seeding KV across 3 PoPs with ~200k keys each will require ~3–4GB of one-time egress and a 30–45 minute pre-warm window depending on network saturation. If demos are back-to-back, pre-warm must happen between windows otherwise cache hits drop off.

Ops overhead and runbook items:
1) Scheduling API to reserve burst slots (Marissa/team should call at least 24 hours out for standard prep; 4 hours is minimum, but 24 preferred).
2) Pre-warm job with an observable playback; success criteria = >95% cache hit at demo start.
3) Emergency fallback: attach lower-cost quantized model variant and route traffic there if burst pool saturates.

I'll draft a short ops playbook if we agree to proceed.

— Jonas
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & sidecar capacity ask

Thanks — procurement/finance view: a few contract & billing flags.

1) SLA exception term: we can support a pilot-level SLA addendum that does not alter enterprise-wide SLAs. Addendum should expire (auto-terminate) after the pilot unless extended. We should include a clause that allows Redwood to switch to a fallback variant if infrastructure is constrained — no penalty to us.

2) Pricing model: recommend a time-and-materials uplift for burst windows (flat per-hour surcharge + overage per 1M tokens). That keeps exposure bounded. Also require a minimum commitment for K hours per month to prevent open-ended burst claims.

3) Operational liability: include a statement that pre-warm success is dependent on customer's ability to provide realistic prefixes and traffic patterns; if they provide inadequate input we'll use best-effort but not guarantee tail latency.

Legal should sign off on the language; I'll draft a short addendum and share a redline.

— Soojin
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T13:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & capacity sidecar ask

Product notes & roadmap impact:
- We can support a short-term sidecar/burst model with two mitigations to minimize platform risk: 1) require the customer to accept a controlled fallback (aggressive quantize) after a hard cap, and 2) surface per-demo telemetry to the customer so they understand hit rates. Both are straightforward to deliver in the next sprint as long as infra provides the pre-warm API.

- Long-term product ask: we should centralize a 'demo mode' feature that automates pre-warm, slot reservation, and fallback routing. This pilot is a good driver for that — I'll add a ticket to the roadmap: DEMO-118 (automated demo-sidecar orchestration).

Operationally, my preference is to limit the burst lanes to scheduled, ticketed windows (no ad-hoc demo guarantees). If EdgeRep wants ad-hoc SLA, we should price heavily and require higher commitment.

— Kimberly
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EdgeRep pilot request — temporary burst SLA & capacity sidecar ask

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team — this is helpful. Carlos, looping you in with the proposed constraints so you can confirm if the pre-warm windows and fallback quantized variant are acceptable.

Action items we agreed on internally:
- Jonas: draft the ops playbook and pre-warm job script (target by 10/23)
- Soojin: draft the SLA addendum + pricing uplift (draft by 10/22)
- Priyom/Kim: consolidate runbook and product ticket DEMO-118, include telemetry hooks (target by 10/25)

Carlos — can you confirm the typical number of prefixes you’ll want pre-seeded and if you can commit to scheduling demo windows at least 24 hours in advance?

If ok, we’ll send a short pilot statement of work and the addendum for signature.

Thanks — Marissa
